title: Granite Systems - Inference Pathfinder Discovery
summary: Introductory discovery focused on how Granite Systems would adopt Redwood: evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deploy modes, time-to-first-token for a sandbox PoC, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and cost/latency tradeoffs. AE to share pricing & quickstart artifacts; SE to run a latency baseline and provide a sample docker-compose for Private. Agreed next steps include a two-week pilot using hosted sandbox credits and a technical deep dive next Tuesday.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
next_steps: Leah to send Hosted sandbox credits instructions, Postman collection, and pricing sheet (by 2025-08-25)
Marco to run a quick latency baseline against a 7B open model and share results + sample config for Dedicated vs Hosted (by 2025-08-26)
Schedule technical deep dive demo for Private deployment with infra team (proposed 2025-08-27)
Granite to provide rough monthly token estimate and compliance checklist answers (by 2025-08-23)
action_items: Leah Brooks: Email sandbox setup steps + Postman collection (due 2025-08-25)
Marco Alvarez: Latency baseline capture and sample Dedicated config (due 2025-08-26)
Iris Chen: Share token/per-day estimate and list of regulatory controls required (due 2025-08-23)
transcript:
00:00 Leah Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
00:05 Iris Chen: Iris here. Hi Leah.
00:07 Mark Davenport: Mark, CTO.
:10 Sofia Ruiz: Sofia here.
00:12 Leah Brooks: Great. Marco from Redwood is on for the technical side.
00:15 Marco Alvarez: Hey all, morning.
00:17 Leah Brooks: High level, today's goal is to understand how you'd like to use Redwood, and figure out a path to get a first working integration — sandbox, quick pilot, whatever makes sense.
00:27 Iris Chen: Yeah, we want something low friction. We have a couple of internal apps that need summarization and retrieval assisted search. Ideally we want to hit an MVP in two weeks.
00:35 Mark Davenport: From infra side, our questions are really: can we start on hosted for speed, when do we need dedicated, and what's involved if we need a Private VPC deploy for compliance. Plus cost — we have to keep an eye on per-token spend.
00:50 Leah Brooks: Perfect. Quick outline: hosted gets you fastest time to first token, we can give sandbox credits and a Postman collection for a quick test. Dedicated is reserved capacity for steady throughput and predictable latency, and Private is VPC/on-prem for stricter controls and KMS integration. Marco can talk about perf and what to expect.
01:10 Marco Alvarez: Yeah, for the models you described, against a 7B variant on hosted infra, typical p95 latency for streaming chat is in the 200-400ms per-token ballpark depending on sequence length; Dedicated removes noisy multitenant variance and gives you queue guarantees. Private adds the networking overhead but gives you control over KMS and egress.
01:35 Sofia Ruiz: Are there published benchmarks we can look at? And what about token pricing comparisons?
01:40 Leah Brooks: I'll send the pricing sheet and our benchmark page — the benchmark link notes model/machine pairings. Also we'll include sample configs and a quickstart script to do a first API call in under 10 minutes.
01:52 Mark Davenport: For compliance, we need SOC2 type II, audit logs, SSO via SAML, and ability to bring our own KMS. Are those supported?
02:00 Marco Alvarez: Yes to all. Hosted supports SOC2 and audit logs; for KMS and on-prem private deploys we have integrations with common KMS providers and an option for a customer-managed control plane. There can be a bit of setup for HSM/KMS exchange, we can share our runbook.
02:18 Iris Chen: Good. One thing — we run some high-QPS bursty jobs for nightly indexing. Would hosted manage that spike or would we need Dedicated?
02:26 Marco Alvarez: Hosted can handle typical bursts but if they're predictable and large it's safer to go Dedicated. We have autoscale and burst credits for Dedicated customers; you also get configurable queue and routing to prevent noisy neighbors.
02:40 Leah Brooks: Curious about timeframe: you said two weeks for MVP — is that from a hosted sandbox or an internal Private install?
02:46 Iris Chen: Hosted sandbox ideally. We need to show business results first before investing in Dedicated or Private.
02:52 Leah Brooks: Great — so path: sandbox -> pilot -> decide Dedicated/Private. We'll give sandbox credits and a sandbox environment so you can test with realistic load.
03:00 Mark Davenport: Can we do an A/B between hosted and a small Dedicated baseline to compare latency and cost?
03:05 Marco Alvarez: Absolutely. We can spin a small Dedicated pool — even a single instance — to run the same payload. We'll provide an apples-to-apples config.
03:12 Sofia Ruiz: What about network security for hosted calls? We need to ensure data residency and limited logging for certain datasets.
03:18 Marco Alvarez: Hosted supports data residency options depending on region; for private datasets we recommend Private deployments. For logging we have redaction options and retention controls and per-token audit logs you can export to your SIEM.
03:30 Iris Chen: Do you have guides for implementing redaction?
03:33 Leah Brooks: Yes — I'll attach our data handling guide.
03:36 Mark Davenport: Another issue is cold start and KV cache warm-up — we need predictable latency for customer-facing features. How does Redwood handle caching?
03:44 Marco Alvarez: We do prefix and KV caching with warm-up heuristics and persistent KV across sessions on Dedicated. That reduces tail latency after the cache is warmed. For hosted, our continuous batching and prefix cache help but Dedicated gives you more persistent cache control.
04:00 Leah Brooks: For the quick pilot, we'll give you a script to exercise endpoints and a Postman collection, plus a sample eval harness. That should get your devs to a first token fast.
04:10 Iris Chen: About credits — is there an expiration and what limits are there?
04:13 Leah Brooks: Sandbox credits typically are good for 30 days; they include a mix of generation and embedding units. We'll detail limits in the email.
04:20 Mark Davenport: Any lock-in on model variants? We prefer being able to swap models or run our own fine-tuned model later.
04:26 Marco Alvarez: You can pin model versions and rollouts. We support bringing in fine-tuned or customer models in Private or Dedicated; hosted has curated model catalog but we can support custom endpoints for enterprise plans.
04:40 Sofia Ruiz: For the private install, what's the packaging? Docker? Helm?
04:44 Marco Alvarez: For Private we provide an on-prem package that can deploy via helm on your k8s cluster or via a docker-compose for air-gapped evals. We'll share the deployment manifest sample.
04:55 Iris Chen: Great. For success metrics, we want 99th percentile latency under 800ms for generative responses and cost under $X per 1k queries. We can hand over our current budget numbers after this call.
05:10 Leah Brooks: That helps. We'll use those as gating criteria for the pilot.
05:15 Mark Davenport: One toss-up: we may have a security review next week — do you have SOC2 docs and penetration testing reports we can share with our security team?
05:24 Marco Alvarez: Yep, we'll provide our SOC2 summary, pen test attestation, and our security whitepaper. Leah will attach those in the follow-up.
05:32 Sofia Ruiz: Onboarding: can devs use an API key or do you recommend an SDK?
05:36 Leah Brooks: Both. For quick integration, Postman or curl with an API key is easiest; we also have SDKs in Python and Node with helpers for streaming.
05:45 Iris Chen: Time to first token — realistically, how fast could a junior dev get from zero to a working example?
05:50 Leah Brooks: With the Postman collection and sandbox creds, we aim for under 30 minutes for a basic text generation sample. Full retrieval integration will take longer, but we have templates.
06:00 Marco Alvarez: If you want data ingestion pipelines, we have a transformer-based ingestion example and an embeddings pipeline with batching that we can share.
06:07 Mark Davenport: For POC telemetry, can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency?
06:12 Marco Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console gives token breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces, and you can tag routes. We'll demo that in the next session.
06:22 Leah Brooks: Okay — let's capture the pilot scope. Two-week sandbox pilot, exercise 3 core flows: summarization, retrieval QA, nightly index. We'll run a small Dedicated comparison. Anyone object?
06:36 Iris Chen: Sounds good.
06:37 Mark Davenport: Agreed.
06:38 Sofia Ruiz: Fine.
06:39 Leah Brooks: Great. Any blockers we haven't covered?
06:42 Mark Davenport: Data residency for EU customers — does Redwood host in eu-west?
06:46 Marco Alvarez: We have EU regions; we'll confirm availability for the specific model and infra pair you want.
06:52 Iris Chen: Also curious about SSO provisioning — we use SAML + Okta.
06:56 Marco Alvarez: Full SAML SSO is supported, we can provide an IdP guide for Okta.
07:00 Leah Brooks: Final recap: Leah will send sandbox creds, Postman, pricing, security pack. Marco will run a quick latency baseline and share Dedicated config. Granite to provide token estimate and compliance checklist. We propose a technical deep dive next Tuesday.
07:14 Mark Davenport: Works for us.
07:16 Iris Chen: Thanks all.
07:17 Leah Brooks: Thanks, bye.
